findings.reason: all five test arms can pass and the section still not deliver its stated saving, so the plan would be dispatched, land green, and go straight into the repair section §7's rule says a failed live gate becomes.
findings.text: §15 keeps the process cache across the three sources it names, but the residual it explicitly retains ("The slow pass already fires only on covered files, names no path, and keeps dropping the build") is the same drop it exists to remove: `_slow_tree` (`reckon/change_streams.py:471-488`) fires on `_walk_discovery_signature` (`reckon/serve.py`, the covered files' count and newest mtime plus three state files), so an HTML file edited, added or removed — case (2), a change the index does cover — and a crew write to `docs/state/<project>/index.json`, the very change §15's Why blames, both still call `_invalidate_tree_views` and clear `_CACHE` within `_CROSS_NODE_SLOW_S` = 60 s. The section's own live clause measures two passes at least 60 s apart, so a slow tick lands inside every measured window and case (2)'s kernel mark and case (3)'s fast-pass mark are both undone, leaving the second pass to pay the ≈2,500-directory stat sweep the section was written to remove

findings.reason: the clause passes whenever no change landed on the measured tree inside the window, and the unfixed code answers that same quiet window just as fast, so the pass it records is not evidence the section's mechanism ran.
findings.text: the section's only measure of the whole mechanism is the live clause "The second pass must answer in under 1 s"; it declares no control, unlike §7's two arms and unlike the five unit arms, and it is satisfied by a window in which no state or covered change landed, so it cannot distinguish a kept build from a window that never exercised the drop

rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the section's end-to-end clause ("The second pass must answer in under 1 s") carries no control and no stated precondition, and the five case arms all drive the read directly, so no arm can fail when the retained slow-pass drop is what makes the second pass slow.
